ruling.recommended_action: Route the file to a Ryde human reviewer: confirm the SAFE-1 threat and handle the account/conduct side; separately, review whether the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee should be upheld (all three NS-1 limbs are recorded as satisfied), and check the driver's 90-day dispute history for a repeated-conduct pattern before any account action.
ruling.reasoning:
The rider complains that the driver threatened her in chat and then cancelled and charged her $6.61 [F4][F7]. Reading the chat in full, the first two messages are ordinary pickup coordination — the driver's arrival notice [F9] and the rider's "2 min, coming" [F10] — but the third message, sent by the driver at 09:54, reads "Hurry up or I will find you and you will regret it." [F11]. In context this is not a pickup arrangement and not a route argument: it is a threat aimed at the rider, sent one minute before the driver cancelled at 09:54:25 [F4]. Under SAFE-1, threats and intimidation in the chat trigger escalation instead of an automatic ruling, so the case cannot be decided as a pure fee dispute [F11][SAFE-1]. I therefore screen this as suspected (the words speak for themselves; the human reviewer decides weight and whether it is confirmed) and do not rule on the merits of the fee [SAFE-1].

On the fee itself I record only what the trace settles, because SAFE-1 bars me from executing an outcome. NS-0 routes this through the driver-cancelled branch [F4][NS-0]. Limbs (i) and (ii) of NS-1 are met on the system record: the driver tapped "I'm Here" at 09:50:45 and was 38 m from the pickup at that moment, inside the 200 m arrival radius [F6][F1][NS-1]. Limb (iii) is also recorded as met: the trace shows 220 s continuously inside the radius after the tap, above the 180 s threshold [F6][NS-1], and the trace further confirms the GPS samples run from the arrival confirmation to the cancellation with no gap beyond the hole threshold [F2][NS-1]. On that record the $6.61 charge would stand as no_action, which is why the rider's argument that limb (iii) fails cannot be accepted as a basis for a refund [F5][F6][NS-1][NS-2].

The rider's remaining points do not change the fee picture but do not save the case from escalation either. The driver's post-trip statement that the rider "kept saying 2 minutes" is a statement, not a system record, and the timestamped chat contains only one such message [F13][F10][F12]; system records override statements, so that part of the driver's account is not relied on. Conversely, the rider's own message [F10] shows she had not boarded, and NS-1 measures the wait from the tap, not from the platform's earlier arrival stamp [F6][F5][NS-1]. If a reviewer concludes the threat is confirmed and/or the no-show wait is not clean, the outcome switches to a full refund of $6.61 [F7][NS-2]; that choice belongs to the human now. The profile fields show one upheld no-show dispute for the driver in 90 days [F18] and none for the rider [F17], but profile facts can never decide a case and cannot alone support a flag here, so no account flag is attached by me [F18][RD-6].

Rejected: NS-1 measures the wait from the arrival confirmation, not from the 09:49:50 platform arrival stamp, and the record shows 3 min 40 s in radius after the tap [F6][F5][F2][NS-1].

Rejected in part: the driver's post-trip statement about repeated '2 minutes' [F13] does not match the timestamped chat [F12][F10], and statements yield to system records; but the rider's own message [F10] shows she had not boarded, so it does not defeat the no-show finding [NS-1].

Rejected: the NS-1 conditions are recorded as satisfied (tap, 38 m at tap, 220 s in radius, no GPS gap) [F6][F1][F2], so on the record the $6.61 is not refundable; any full refund under NS-2 is now for the human reviewer given the SAFE-1 escalation [F7][NS-2][SAFE-1].
Accepted in substance: the 09:54 message [F11] is a threat and forces escalation under SAFE-1, so no automatic ruling is made [F11][F4][SAFE-1].
Accepted: the chat record is complete and every message timestamped [F12], so the threat and the rider's reply can be read in full and there is no G12 completeness gap.

Rejected as a basis for a flag: the driver's single upheld 90-day dispute is a no-show [F18], which may become relevant only if the reviewer finds repeated conduct; profile facts cannot alone decide or flag this case [F18][F17][RD-6]. No flag_account is set by this ruling.

Rejected as a request for no_action: the trace does support the NS-1 conditions [F6][F2][F3], but SAFE-1 forbids an automatic fee ruling once the threat in [F11] appears, so the file goes to a human [SAFE-1].
Rejected: the fee cannot be finally confirmed automatically while the SAFE-1 threat screen stands; the reviewer decides the fee together with the safety element [F11][F7][SAFE-1][NS-1].
